description: A Sanskrit reading platform for Patanjali's Yoga Sutras with sandhi splitting, dictionary lookup, and offline-first architecture. Phase 1 MVP + Phase 2 enhancements.

userStories.title: Database schema and models
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the database schema to store texts, sections, blocks, and dictionary entries so data persists correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: Create SQLAlchemy models: Text, TextSection, TextBlock, Dictionary, DictionaryEntry
Text has slug, title, description fields
TextSection has slug, title, order, foreign key to Text
TextBlock has content (Devanagari), content_transliteration (IAST), content_meaning (English), word_analysis (JSON), commentary, order, foreign key to TextSection
Dictionary has name, code (e.g., 'mw', 'apte')
DictionaryEntry has key (SLP1), value (definition), foreign key to Dictionary
SQLite database created at data/yoga_sutras.db
All models have proper relationships and indexes
userStories.notes: Generic text hierarchy supports future texts (Bhagavad Gita, Ramayana)

userStories.title: Data scraping and seeding pipeline
userStories.description: As a developer, I need scripts to scrape Yoga Sutras from shlokam.org and seed dictionary data from Cologne (CDSL) so the database is populated.
acceptanceCriteria: Create scripts/scrape_text.py that scrapes all 196 sutras from shlokam.org
Output saved to data/yoga_sutras.json with Devanagari, IAST, and English translation
Create scripts/seed_dictionaries.py that downloads MW and Apte XML from CDSL
Parse XML and populate DictionaryEntry table with SLP1 keys
Create scripts/populate_db.py that loads yoga_sutras.json into Text/Section/Block tables
All 4 Padas created as TextSections (Samadhi, Sadhana, Vibhuti, Kaivalya)
All 196 sutras created as TextBlocks with correct ordering
Scripts are idempotent (can run multiple times safely)

userStories.title: Backend text API service
userStories.description: As a frontend developer, I need REST APIs to fetch texts, sections, and blocks so I can display them in the UI.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/texts returns list of all texts with metadata
GET /api/texts/{slug} returns full text with sections (without blocks for performance)
GET /api/texts/{slug}/section/{section_slug} returns section with all blocks
GET /api/texts/{slug}/block/{block_id} returns single block with full details
All endpoints return proper JSON with consistent structure
Error handling for 404 (not found) cases
Flask app runs on localhost:5000
CORS enabled for frontend development

userStories.title: Backend dictionary lookup service
userStories.description: As a reader, I need an API to look up Sanskrit words so I can understand their meanings from authoritative sources.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/dictionary/{word} returns definitions from all dictionaries
Accepts word in Devanagari, IAST, or SLP1 encoding
Uses indic-transliteration library for script conversion
Returns structured response with dictionary name, key, and definition
Supports fuzzy matching using rapidfuzz for typo tolerance
Response time under 200ms for dictionary lookups
Returns empty array (not error) when word not found
userStories.notes: Dictionary keys stored in SLP1 internally

userStories.title: Backend sandhi splitting service
userStories.description: As a reader, I need compound Sanskrit words split into components so I can understand each part individually.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/split/{compound} returns list of possible splits
Integrates Vidyut Cheda for sandhi splitting via vidyut-py
Accepts input in Devanagari or IAST
Returns splits with both Devanagari and IAST representations
Graceful fallback when Vidyut cannot split (return original word)
Vidyut data directory configured at data/vidyut-data/
Each split component is individually lookupable in dictionary
userStories.notes: Example: yogashchittavrittinirodhah -> yogah + chitta + vritti + nirodhah

userStories.title: Frontend project setup and navigation
userStories.description: As a user, I need a React frontend with navigation so I can browse the Yoga Sutras by Pada and Sutra number.
acceptanceCriteria: Create React + TypeScript + Tailwind project in frontend/ directory
Home page shows welcome message and quick navigation to any Pada
Sidebar or tab navigation for 4 Padas (Samadhi, Sadhana, Vibhuti, Kaivalya)
Each Pada page shows list of sutras with numbers and first line preview
Clicking a sutra navigates to full sutra view
Previous/Next navigation between sutras within a Pada
Responsive design works on desktop and mobile
API calls configured to backend at localhost:5000

userStories.title: Frontend sutra display with word interaction
userStories.description: As a reader, I want to see each sutra with Devanagari, transliteration, and translation, with clickable words for lookup.
acceptanceCriteria: Sutra view shows Devanagari text in large, readable Noto Sans Devanagari font
IAST transliteration displayed below Devanagari
English translation displayed below transliteration
Each word in Devanagari text is individually clickable
Clicking a word triggers dictionary lookup
Visual hover state indicates words are clickable
Commentary section is collapsible (hidden by default)
Sutra number and Pada clearly indicated
userStories.notes: Word boundaries may need sandhi analysis to determine

userStories.title: Frontend dictionary panel
userStories.description: As a reader, I want a dictionary panel that shows word definitions when I click a word so I can understand meanings in context.
acceptanceCriteria: Dictionary panel slides in from right side on desktop
Dictionary panel shows as bottom sheet on mobile
Displays clicked word in Devanagari and IAST
Shows Monier-Williams definition with formatting preserved
Shows Apte definition in separate section
Indicates grammar info (gender, case) when available
Close button to dismiss panel
Loading state while fetching definition
Not found state when word has no dictionary entry
userStories.notes: Panel should not block sutra text on desktop

userStories.title: Frontend sandhi splitting integration
userStories.description: As a reader, I want compound words automatically split so I can look up each component separately.
acceptanceCriteria: When clicking a compound word, show split options before dictionary
Display split components with visual separators (+ sign)
Each component is clickable for individual dictionary lookup
Show original compound above the split
Option to view dictionary for full compound (unsplit)
Visual indication when a word is compound vs simple
Graceful handling when split fails (show original word)
userStories.notes: Pre-compute splits for known sutras in word_analysis JSON field

userStories.title: Full-text search across sutras
userStories.description: As a reader, I want to search across all sutras in both Sanskrit and English so I can find relevant passages.
acceptanceCriteria: Search input in header/navigation area
Searches across Devanagari, IAST, and English translation
Uses fuzzy matching for typo tolerance
Results show sutra number, matching text highlighted, and context
Clicking result navigates to full sutra view
Search as you type with debouncing (300ms)
Empty state when no results found
Backend endpoint: GET /api/search?q={query}
userStories.notes: Use rapidfuzz on backend for fuzzy matching

userStories.title: Bookmarks and favorites
userStories.description: As a reader, I want to bookmark sutras so I can quickly return to important passages.
acceptanceCriteria: Bookmark icon on each sutra view
Clicking bookmark toggles saved state (filled/unfilled icon)
Bookmarks page shows all saved sutras
Bookmarks stored in browser localStorage
Bookmarks persist across sessions
Can remove bookmark from bookmarks page
Show count of bookmarks in navigation
Export bookmarks as JSON (optional)
userStories.notes: No backend storage needed - client-side only for MVP

userStories.title: Transliteration toggle
userStories.description: As a reader, I want to toggle between different script displays so I can read in my preferred format.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings toggle for script preference: Devanagari, IAST, or Both
Toggle persists in localStorage
Sutra display respects script preference
Dictionary panel respects script preference
Search works regardless of script preference
Toggle accessible from header or settings menu
Default to Both (Devanagari + IAST)
userStories.notes: Use indic-transliteration for conversions if needed client-side

userStories.title: PWA offline support
userStories.description: As a reader, I want the app to work offline so I can study without internet connection.
acceptanceCriteria: Service worker registered and caches app shell
All 196 sutras available offline after initial load
Dictionary data cached for offline lookup
Offline indicator shown when disconnected
App installable as PWA on mobile devices
manifest.json with proper icons and metadata
Cache invalidation strategy for updates
Offline mode gracefully handles failed API calls

userStories.title: Docker deployment configuration
userStories.description: As a developer, I need Docker configuration so the app can be deployed to the homelab Kubernetes cluster.
acceptanceCriteria: Dockerfile for backend (Python/Flask)
Dockerfile for frontend (Node build + nginx serve)
docker-compose.yml for local development
Environment variables for configuration
Health check endpoints for both services
Production-ready nginx configuration
Database and data files mounted as volumes
Images build successfully and containers start
userStories.notes: Deploy to homelab K8s after Docker setup verified
